title: gofmt in go1.26.5 gives different output on amd64 and arm64, which breaks ci-kubernetes-verify-master-canary
content:
### Which jobs are failing?

ci-kubernetes-verify-master-canary (the only verify job that runs on arm64 nodes, on the AKS build cluster)

### Which tests are failing?

verify-gofmt.sh

### Since when has it been failing?

First failure 2026-07-20 17:12 UTC, a few hours after #140000 merged. The job then alternated between green and red depending on which node it landed on. It has failed every run since 2026-07-29 17:06 UTC because every pod since then has landed on arm64 nodes.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-k8s-infra-canaries#verify-master-canary

### Reason for failure (if possible)

gofmt from go1.26.5 does not produce the same output on amd64 and arm64 for one struct literal in `pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodevolumelimits/csi.go` (added in #140000). The amd64 build of gofmt accepts the code as checked in. The arm64 build wants the short fields aligned to the long `enableInPlacePodVerticalScalingSchedulerPreemption` line. Each build rejects the form the other one wants, so running update-gofmt cannot produce a form both accept.

This is a bug in Go, not in the release binaries. The gofmt binaries in the CI image match the official go.dev tarballs, and building gofmt from unmodified go1.26.5 sources reproduces the difference purely by changing GOARCH. The cause is in go/printer, which decides where to break column alignment using a geometric mean computed with `math.Log` and `math.Exp` (nodes.go lines 232 to 287 in go1.26.5). Those functions can differ in the last bit between architectures, and the field lengths in this literal sit exactly on the 2.5 ratio threshold, so the decision flips. Presubmits run on amd64, which is why the change merged cleanly.

Evidence: the last green run (build 2082497666687700992, amd64 node) and the first red run of the streak (build 2082513014723973120, arm64 node) tested the same commit 7fbcad5e8ec.

### Anything else we need to know?

The fix on our side is to restructure the literal so the long field is assigned after the struct is built. I verified that form is accepted by gofmt from go1.26.5 on linux amd64, linux arm64, and darwin arm64, and by go1.27rc2. I will send a PR and file a golang/go issue for the printer bug.

title: cpumanager:staticpolicy:smtalign: pod admission failed after kubelet restart
content:
### What happened?

When Kubelet is configured with `static` CPUManager policy + `full-pcpus-only` option, after kubelet restart, pod is not get admitted and  I'm getting the following error under kubelet logs:

```
Dec 04 12:42:25 kubenswrapper[2410667]: I1204 12:42:25.173086 2410667 kubelet.go:2320] "Pod admission denied" podUID="4355ee04-54b0-4755-b23e-d05ce12e54c1" pod="my-app-namespace/app-deployment" reason="SMTAlignmentError" message="SMT Alignment Error: not enough free physical CPUs: available physical CPUs = 1, requested CPUs = 2, CPUs per core = 1"
```

After manually deleting and recreating the pod, it gets admitted, so the claim that there are node enough free physical CPUs is wrong.


Pod spec:

```yaml

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2024-12-04T12:50:20Z"
  name: app-deployment
  namespace: my-app-namespace
  resourceVersion: "11109192"
  uid: 16737fd6-45e1-4371-b10e-3eff1377c224
spec:
  containers:
  - args:
    - while true; do sleep 10000; done;
    command:
    - /bin/sh
    - -c
    image: quay.io/jitesoft/alpine
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    name: app-container2
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 100Mi
      requests:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 100Mi
  qosClass: Guaranteed

```

### What did you expect to happen?

After kubelet restart pod should readmitted 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
On a node with 4 CPUs:
 `1` reserved (`reserverSystemCPUs`)
 `3` allocatable

1. Configure CPUManager to `static` and `full-pcpus-only` option to `true`
2. Create a Guaranteed QoS class pod requesting 2  exclusive CPUs:
``` yaml
kind: Pod
...
spec:
  containers:
...
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 100Mi
      requests:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 100Mi
```
3. wait for pod to start
4. restart kubelet
5. Pod will failed with SMTAlignment error

NOTE:
It's possible to reproduce the issue on a system with any size of CPUs.
A general formula would be:
On a node with `N` CPUs:
 `1` reserved 
 `N-1` allocatable
Create a Guaranteed QoS class pod requesting `N / 2`  exclusive CPUs:

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

I faced the same problem, but with apiserver.
The most annoying in this case, that kubelet is trying to allocate a new cpuset before removing the previous container.
And, if get the SMT Align Error, it never will try to recreate the pod after.

How to reproduce:
1. install cluster with kind:
```
❯ kind create cluster
Creating cluster "kind" ...
 ✓ Ensuring node image (kindest/node:v1.32.2) 🖼
```

2. enter control-plane node:
```
docker exec -ti $(docker ps | grep kind-control-plane | awk '{print $1}') bash
```

3. stop kubelet
```
systemctl stop kubelet
```

4. check cpu in container:
```
lscpu | grep 'On-line'
  On-line CPU(s) list:       0-13
```

5. Choose cpu for reqs/limits:  
in my case it's 14 / 2 = 7, so I choose 8 to have more than half of the whole cpus amount (to receive SMT error)

6. Change apiserver reqs/limits:
```
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 8
          memory: 512Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 8
          memory: 512Mi
```

7. Add the following settings to the kubelet config:
```
reservedSystemCPUs: '0'
cpuManagerPolicy: static
cpuManagerPolicyOptions:
  distribute-cpus-across-numa: "true"
  full-pcpus-only: "true"
featureGates:
  CPUManager: true
  CPUManagerPolicyAlphaOptions: true
  CPUManagerPolicyBetaOptions: true
  CPUManagerPolicyOptions: true
```

8. Delete cpu_manager_state:
```
rm -f /var/lib/kubelet/cpu_manager_state
```

8. Start kubelet:
```
systemctl restart kubelet
```

9. Check if apiserver works and got it's cpuset:
```
cat /var/lib/kubelet/cpu_manager_state
```

10. Restart kubelet and check it's log for SMT align error.  
After the restart kubelet also will delete the previous container, and never recreate it, even after the `RemoveStaleState` stage and returning back the apiserver cpuset into the default one.

title: unit-master-dependencies: TestCelCostStability fails with cel-go v0.30.0 because runtime costs changed
content:
### Which jobs are failing?

ci-kubernetes-unit-dependencies

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-arch-code-organization#unit-master-dependencies

### Which tests are failing?

- TestCelCostStability/listMap_access/self.listMap.exists(m,_m.v2_==_'z') (runtime cost 22, expected 24)
- TestCelCostStability/listMap_access/!self.listMap.all(m,_m.v2_!=_'z') (runtime cost 20, expected 22)

Package: k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/schema/cel

### Since when has it been failing?

2026-07-26. The last green run started at 00:19 UTC and the first red run started at 04:19 UTC. Both runs tested the same kubernetes commit, so the cause is outside our repo.

### Reason for failure

The job updates every dependency to the latest release before running the unit tests. cel-go v0.30.0 was published at 03:54 UTC on 2026-07-26, inside that window.

In cel-go v0.30.0, cel-expr/cel-go#1369 changed `==`, `!=`, and strict binary calls so they stop before evaluating the right hand side when the left hand side is an error. The cost observer in cel-go only charges a call when it has seen all of the argument values, so these calls stopped being charged. Both failing expressions compare a field that is unset on two of the three list elements, so each one now reports a cost that is lower by 2.

Costs only went down. That is safe for existing CRDs because the compatibility rule only forbids cost increases. It still breaks these tests because they pin exact values.

### Anything else we need to know?

I proposed a fix upstream in cel-expr/cel-go#1394. It keeps the lazy evaluation from #1369 and only fixes the cost accounting. With that fix applied on top of v0.30.0, the full k8s schema/cel test package passes with no changes on our side.

There are two ways to make the job green:

1. Upstream accepts cel-expr/cel-go#1394 and cuts a patch release from the v0.30.0 base. We then bump to that release with no test changes.
2. We bump to cel-go v0.30.0 as it is and update the two pinned values. I have this ready as well.

One more warning. Testing our suite against current cel-go master (past v0.30.0) shows more cost changes coming in the next release: one optMap expression goes up from 8 to 9 at runtime, and four estimated costs go up as well (for example 22 to 31). Increases are the direction our compatibility rule forbids, so we should raise this upstream before v0.31.0 is cut.

/kind failing-test
/sig api-machinery
/sig architecture
/area dependency

title: Failure cluster [08ffb694...] `StatefulSet` problems in `ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary`
content: ### Failure cluster [08ffb694187fb53f5d54](https://go.k8s.io/triage#08ffb694187fb53f5d54) ##### Error text: ``` [FAILED] Failed waiting for pods to enter running: context deadline exceeded In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/statefulset/wait.go:63 @ 07/10/26 16:56:53.526 ``` #### Recent failures: [7/23/2026, 8:56:30 PM ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2080456944480423936) [7/23/2026, 12:55:33 PM ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2080335900859961344) [7/23/2026, 4:56:29 AM ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2080215099477331968) [7/22/2026, 8:55:20 PM ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2080094057907884032) [7/22/2026, 12:53:54 PM ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2079973098446131200) /kind failing-test /sig apps --- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-testing-kind#kind-master-alpha-beta-features-canary 🤖 please dig into this ## Root cause: PR #140350 un-skipped three heavyweight `[Slow]` StatefulSet tests that then time out — this is a **test-selection regression, not a product bug** ### TL;DR On **2026-07-10** the `feature.StatefulSet` label was removed from the "Deploy clustered applications" tests (CockroachDB / MySQL / ZooKeeper) in [PR #140350 "Drop unnecessary sig-apps e2e features"](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140350) (@soltysh, merged 14:05 UTC). Those tests were **skipped** before and now **run** in jobs that filter by `Feature:` — where they consistently time out at ~620s waiting for the app pods to come up. Cluster [`08ffb694…`](https://go.k8s.io/triage#08ffb694187fb53f5d54) is this, across three jobs. ### Regression boundary (job `ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary`) | | Build | Started | SHA | |---|---|---|---| | Last green | [`2075496600431497216`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2075496600431497216) | 2026-07-10 08:25Z | `0fe889a7` | | First red | [`2075617650255335424`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2075617650255335424) | 2026-07-10 16:26Z | `a473cbba` | Solid red streak ever since (all 40+ builds through 7/24). Commit window `0fe889a7..a473cbba` = 6 PRs; only #140350 touches these tests. ### Smoking gun — junit shows the flip precisely - **Green build junit:** `[sig-apps] StatefulSet Deploy clustered applications [Feature:StatefulSet] should creating a working CockroachDB cluster [Slow]` → **`status="skipped"`** - **Red build junit** ([`2080456944…`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary/2080456944480423936)): same test, now **without** the `[Feature:StatefulSet]` tag → **`status="failed" time="620"`**, error: ``` [FAILED] Failed waiting for pods to enter running: context deadline exceeded k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/statefulset/wait.go:63 ``` ### The change ([diff](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140350/files)) `test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go`: ```diff - f.Describe("Deploy clustered applications", feature.StatefulSet, framework.WithSlow(), func() { + f.Describe("Deploy clustered applications", framework.WithSlow(), func() { ``` plus deletion of `feature.StatefulSet`/`feature.StatefulUpgrade` from `test/e2e/feature/feature.go`. **Mechanism:** the kind canary job selects with `LABEL_FILTER: "Feature: isSubsetOf OffByDefault && !Deprecated && !Flaky && !Serial"` (`config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-testing/kubernetes-kind-ci.yaml`). With `[Feature:StatefulSet]` present (not an off-by-default gate), the test was excluded; strip the label and it now satisfies the filter and executes. The two kops jobs skip `[Feature:…]` classically, so the same relabel un-skips them there too. ### Breadth confirms it's the tests, not infra Same three tests, same signature, failing concurrently across all three jobs in the cluster — kind-alpha-beta-features-canary plus [`e2e-ci-kubernetes-kops-cos-gce-slow-canary`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/e2e-ci-kubernetes-kops-cos-gce-slow-canary/2080482366580592640) and `e2e-ci-kubernetes-kops-al2023-aws-slow-canary`. The BeforeEach (client, namespace, service account) succeeds; only the app-pods-running wait times out. This rules out node/registry/kind-startup infra failure and rules out a code regression in a component — nothing in the StatefulSet controller changed in the window. ### Classification **Real, datable test regression** (onset 7/10, single causative PR) — but the defect is in **test gating**, not in Kubernetes itself. These CockroachDB/MySQL/ZooKeeper deployments are known-heavy and were intentionally feature-gated so they only run where opted in; the cleanup PR removed the gate without accounting for the label-filter jobs that relied on it. ### Suggested fix directions (for sig-apps / @soltysh) - Re-gate the "Deploy clustered applications" block (restore a `[Feature:…]`/off-by-default label or tag them `[Flaky]`/`[Serial]` so the canary filters exclude them), **or** - Add a job-level skip for these three tests, **or** - If they are meant to run, raise the StatefulSet running timeout for these apps. No existing tracking/fix/revert PR found as of this triage. cc @soltysh @pohly (job owner, `testgrid-alert-email: patrick.ohly@intel.com`). --- *🔬 Automated triage on behalf of @dims, generated by Claude with the `k8s-ci-triage` skill. May contain mistakes — verify before acting.* cc @soltysh /assign /triage accepted /priority important-soon @dims those tests indeed need investigation, I'll look if I can make them working, if not I'll disable them. After #140982 merged https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-alpha-beta-features-canary got back to green, so we're good 🎉

title: How to make cluster-concepts (e.g. ServiceCIDR) become tenant-friendly?
content:
I testing with ServiceCIDR to add additional ranges, it works, but i can't find how can i control which cidr will be used on assigning the next clusterIP if one or more cidr have free addresses.
Are there an annotation for that?

---

/sig network

@pasztorl the initial feature is only focused on solving the problem of IP exhaustion, similar you add new disks to solve the storage exhaustion problems, here you add new IP blocks.

We are getting now more request for people trying to also express affinity for these blocks, once the feature is GA after 1.33, if there are strong use cases and well defined we can look for extending the feature, but for implementing something we need to carefully design it as the failure mode can be complex.

@pasztorl can you please describe better your user stories, how do you plan to use it? what happen if the one you select does no longer have free ips, do you fall back or do you fail?

What I essentially did was a multi-tenant test. I designated namespaces that each receive a separate IP range. There are VPN endpoints that can see specific network ranges, which also helps separate them.

Since it's currently not configurable which IP range services receive their addresses from, I solved this using a mutating webhook. The webhook modifies the service and adds the spec.clusterIP before it gets created.

This worked, but I noticed that services created in other namespaces also started receiving IPs from the previuosly create servicecidr  range. It seemed as if the last allocated IP range became the default for the next assignment. (?)

I think a clean solution would be to follow what Cilium does with [multi-pool IPAM](https://docs.cilium.io/en/latest/network/concepts/ipam/multi-pool/); using an annotation  (on namespace or pod) to determine which range a given pod gets its IP from. Applying this approach to services would be great.

If a servicecidr runs out of available IPs and it's explicitly required that IPs must be allocated from that CIDR, I suggest preventing the service from being created and instead returning an error.

Also if there is no annotation use the default cidr.

I know, this is a different approach than what it was originally designed for. For me, the goal is not to extend an existing range, but I completely understand the approach where a filling default CIDR range can be easily extended, but fundamentally, I think the issue now is that if there are multiple service CIDRs, it is not predictable where the next IP address will be allocated from.


> This worked, but I noticed that services created in other namespaces also started receiving IPs from the previuosly create servicecidr range. It seemed as if the last allocated IP range became the default for the next assignment. (?)

I see, this is something the multi-network group is working on but that may work for some test or bespoke environment because kubernetes networking model assumes all PodIPs are reachable

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/#the-kubernetes-network-model

You my compartmentalize the ClusterIP in namespaces, but then you need to figure out how the rest of kubernetes features work on that environment, what happens with dns, with webhooks that depend on services, with the kubernetes.default service ... I'm not saying that can;t be done, actually there is people working on that, but what I'm saying is that all those questions  need to be answer... and I do not think we are going to rely on annotations for this, is handy for some things but for more complex APIs like this has a lot of troubles



i tested this with cilium and all worked fine. so pods can communicate with other pods using another podcidr and this also works with services too. of course if the other pod/service is in another cidr it using the default gateway and it's IP not NATed.

to fix the unpredictable ip assignment with multiple servicecirds i ended up creating a global mutatingwebhook which kick on service creation. i will follow the future of servicecidrs i hope some time admin can decide more precise how ips assigned from multiple cidrs.






> to fix the unpredictable ip assignment with multiple servicecirds i ended up creating a global mutatingwebhook which kick on service creation. i will follow the future of servicecidrs i hope some time admin can decide more precise how ips assigned from multiple cidrs.

If you want to treat it as a tenanted-resource, you need more than just
affinity per namespace, you need a way to prevent other namespaces from
using it.  IOW it is not just affinity it's another form of "taint".

If I were starting a KEP on this. I might think about how to describe a
per-namespace (or group of namespace) policy which could be consumed by the
service IP allocation logic.  Something along the lines of "this namespace
can use CIDRs labelled tenant=abc123"

It's not clear to me whether that should be part of the CIDR object or
something more like a "binding".

We don't have a for mal concept of tenant, but it seems pretty
uncontentious that it is described by unique values of a known label on
namespaces.

title: [Scheduling] Fast Host-Scoped Inter-Pod Affinity and Anti-Affinity
content:
### What would you like to be added?

The current implementation of inter-pod affinity and anti-affinity in the Kubernetes scheduler is designed for a generic case where a pod's constraints may affect any other pod in the cluster. This results in expensive global scans and map constructions during every scheduling cycle, which can lead to performance bottlenecks.

We propose to optimize the performance of a common use case: host-scoped rules where the `topologyKey` is `kubernetes.io/hostname`.

The core idea is to isolate host-scoped rules from broader topology calculations to **avoid unnecessary cluster-wide scans**.

1.  **Enhanced Caching Layer**: Update the scheduler's `NodeInfo` and `NodeInfoLister` to explicitly track pods with non-host-scoped rules. This allows the scheduler to quickly identify only the specific nodes that require expensive cross-node topology calculations.
2.  **Term Separation**: During the `PreFilter` phase, the plugin should split affinity and anti-affinity terms into two groups: `hostScoped` (hostname) and `nonHostScoped` (all others).
3.  **Localized Filtering**: For host-scoped rules, bypass the construction of global topology maps. Instead, perform a local check against the pods on the specific node being evaluated during the `Filter` phase. This replaces global lookups with a much faster local check.
4.  **Self-Affinity Handling**: Implement a global fallback for host-scoped affinity to handle "first pod" scheduling scenarios (e.g., the first pod in a Deployment). This ensures that the initial pod in a collection can be scheduled efficiently without requiring a global scan.



### Why is this needed?

Host-scoped inter-pod affinity is a very common use case. This is especially true for anti-affinity, where it's not uncommon to have a requirement to not schedule pods of certain workloads on the same node, or to have a "one pod per node" deployment.

With this optimization, host-scoped inter-pod affinity rules can be used without the performance hit of cluster-wide scans, and need less CPU cycles.

🤖 please dig into this. cc @kannon92 ## Triage: `ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial` flakiness (#140944) **TL;DR:** This is **not a single regression** — it's a job that is red ~87% of the time because of an **accumulation of several independent, mostly-intermittent `[Serial]` test failures** on top of a genuinely low pass rate. There is no clean green→red boundary to bisect; instead there is a dominant per-test flake plus a couple of already-tracked failing tests. This is distinct from the related regression #140848, which does **not** affect this lane. ### Evidence **Job health (last 60 builds, ~30 days):** 8 SUCCESS / 52 FAILURE ≈ **13% pass rate**. Greens are sparse and scattered (e.g. builds [2081137182667444224](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial/2081137182667444224), 2080774540123705344, 2076966556100726784) — all three greens have **0 failures out of 1281 testcases**, so when the environment cooperates the whole suite passes. That rules out a persistent code regression and points to intermittency. **No datable onset (Phase 1, Rule 2).** Per-build junit (`junit_fedora01.xml`) shows a *different* set of failing tests almost every run, and the top offender was already failing on **2026-06-27** (build [2070981174641037312](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial/2070981174641037312), 3 HugePages fails) — i.e. well before any recent regression window. No inflection point → this is flakiness, not a regression. **Dominant flake — Pod Level HugePages Resources** (17 failures across 21 sampled reds, the single biggest contributor): ``` [FAILED] Timed out after 30.001s. expected hugepages 1, but found 0 In [JustBeforeEach] at: test/e2e_node/hugepages_test.go:230 ``` This is the host-reservation setup step (`waitForHugepages` / `setHugepages`, [hugepages_test.go:215-233](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/hugepages_test.go#L215)) timing out at 30s waiting for the node to expose reserved hugepage capacity after reconfiguring the host. In green runs all 18 HugePages cases pass — consistent with a flaky/slow host hugepage reservation rather than a broken assertion. **Other recurring contributors (all pre-existing / independently tracked):** - `Ensure Credential Pulled Images … [FeatureGate:KubeletEnsureSecretPulledImages]` — already tracked in **#137004** (`kind/failing-test`, `triage/accepted`). - `Device Plugin`, `POD Resources API`, `ImageGarbageCollect`, `MemoryQoS`, `GarbageCollect` — each appears 1–3× with no fixed onset (background disruptive/serial flakiness). - Occasional cascade builds (e.g. [2077147777527189504](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial/2077147777527189504), 17 fails) where 7 failures share `Failed to get successful response from /configz` — a kubelet-restart timeout that knocks out subsequent serial tests in the same run. ### This is NOT #140848 Issue #140848 (kubelet panic when `PodLevelResourcesFixDefaulting` is enabled but `PodLevelResources` disabled, from #140514, onset 2026-07-22) breaks the **CPU Manager / Memory Manager** suites. This job **explicitly skips those suites** — its config carries `--skip-regex=…\|[Feature:CPUManager]\|[Feature:MemoryManager]\|…` ([node-kubelet.yaml:295](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/master/config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-node/node-kubelet.yaml#L255)) and runs with `PodLevelResources=true`, so the panic mechanism cannot fire here. The onset also predates 07-22. ### Job config (verified, not inferred) `ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial` — CRI-O, `--parallelism=1`, `--focus=[Serial]`, feature gate `PodLevelResources=true`, cluster `k8s-infra-prow-build`, 12h interval, 300m timeout ([node-kubelet.yaml:255-312](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/master/config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-node/node-kubelet.yaml#L255)). ### Classification & recommendation **Flaky lane, multiple independent causes — no single culprit PR to revert.** Suggested next steps for sig-node: 1. **Prioritize the HugePages flake** (biggest single contributor): make `waitForHugepages`/`setHugepages` more robust — the 30s `Eventually` for host hugepage reservation appears too tight under CRI-O/serial load. Owner context: recent churn in this file (#f925e555483, #4b698656bec). 2. Fold the credential-pulled-images failures into existing **#137004**. 3. Investigate the intermittent `/configz context deadline exceeded` cascades (kubelet restart slowness under CRI-O) — same signature family as closed #137995/#139391. **Confidence:** High that this is flakiness (proven: sparse-but-clean greens, no onset, per-build failure sets vary). The HugePages root cause (slow host reservation vs. a code issue) is *suspected* — the definitive check is re-running the HugePages `[Serial]` cases in isolation on a CRI-O node and watching `/proc/meminfo` hugepage counts during `configureHugePages`. `/sig node` *(Note: #140848 is already tracked separately; nothing here overlaps @dims's earlier automated context on this thread.)* --- *🔬 Automated triage on behalf of @dims, generated by Claude with the `k8s-ci-triage` skill. title: [Failing Test] Windows e2e node CPUManager specs failing since 2026-07-17 (windows-e2e-node-master)
content:
### Which jobs are failing?

- `ci-kubernetes-e2enode-windows-master` (every run since 2026-07-17T23:50 UTC; last green 2026-07-17T15:49 UTC)
- `pull-kubernetes-e2enode-windows` (every PR run since 2026-07-19, regardless of PR content)

### Which tests are failing?

All 12 `[sig-windows] [Feature:CPUManager] [Feature:Windows]` specs in `test/e2e_node_windows`, e.g.:

- `should not set CPU affinity on a burstable container` — fails with `burstable container must not receive exclusive CPU affinity: got 0 CPUs (host has 8)`
- `should set CPU affinity with exactly 1 CPU for a single-container pod` (and the 2/3-CPU, multi-container, init-container, and strict-cpu-reservation variants) — all `Timed out after 30.000s` waiting for affinity to appear.

`getWindowsContainerCPUAffinity` reads `ContainerStatus().Status.Resources.Windows.AffinityCpus` via CRI and gets an empty set for every container, i.e. the kubelet is no longer applying any Windows CPU group affinity (`WindowsCPUAndMemoryAffinity` / static CPU manager path via `PreCreateContainer` → `AffinityCpus`).

Because the failing specs each burn 30–77s and the suite is run as plain `go test` (10m default timeout), cmd/go kills the process (`*** Test killed: ran too long (11m0s)`), so junit/ginkgo reports are lost and the job surface just shows a timeout. Fix for that masking: kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing PR adding an explicit `--timeout`.

### Since when has it been failing?

Onset between periodic runs 2078145122851098624 (green, started 2026-07-17T15:49:43Z) and 2078266162692493312 (first red, started 2026-07-17T23:50:41Z).

### Reason for failure (regression window analysis)

kubernetes/kubernetes merges in the window (green clone ~16:04 UTC → red clone ~23:55 UTC):

- #140682 (job controller dead-code removal), #140667 (scheduler unit test), #140150 (docs), #138833 / #138831 (kube-proxy ipvs/ipset prealloc, linux-only), #140497 (coredns manifest bump)

None touch kubelet, CRI, winstats, or the Windows tests → the k/k commit window is effectively empty.

Everything else pinned/unchanged across the boundary:

- kubernetes-sigs/windows-testing: no commits since 2026-07-09
- containerd: pinned 1.7.16
- Go on the VM: 1.26.4 on both sides of the boundary
- test images (busybox 1.37.0-2, pause 3.8): pinned digests

The one moving part is the Azure VM image: `MicrosoftWindowsServer:WindowsServer:2022-datacenter-core-smalldisk-g2:latest`. The first red run's node reports `KernelVersion: 10.0.20348.5386` (July 2026 WS2022 cumulative update; July Patch Tuesday was 2026-07-14, and marketplace image rollout lands ~that week). Green runs never dump Node Info so the prior build isn't in the logs, but the timing matches the image rollout window exactly.

Working hypothesis: the WS2022 July 2026 CU (OS build 20348.5386) changes behavior under the kubelet's Windows CPU affinity path — either winstats CPU topology discovery (`GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx`) returning something the CPU manager can't use, or HCS/job-object group affinity application/reporting — so no `AffinityCpus` ever reach the container.

### Suggested next steps

1. Repro on an Azure VM with the current image; collect kubelet.log (job currently only scps `c:/Logs/*.xml`).
2. Pin the job image to the previous exact version (`az vm image list --all` for the sku, use `:<previous-version>` instead of `:latest`) to confirm/unblock CI.
3. Compare winstats topology output between 20348 builds.

ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary/2080903645343256576) /kind failing-test /sig node --- 🤖 please dig into this! ## Suite-timeout in `ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary` — capacity exhaustion, not a probe regression **TL;DR:** Cluster [`3aa867c5…`](https://go.k8s.io/triage#3aa867c5ba978edcc4ae) is **not** a bug in the liveness/startup-probe tests. It is a **whole-suite ginkgo timeout** (`[TIMEDOUT] A suite timeout occurred`). The `container_probe.go` specs named in the signature are *victims*, not the cause — they're simply the slowest specs, so they're the ones still running when the deadline fires. The real problem: this canary job runs **all of NodeConformance in ~75 min of ginkgo budget, and the suite has grown to the point where it no longer reliably fits.** It fails intermittently whenever the run is a bit slower than average. ### Evidence **1. The failure is a suite deadline, not an assertion.** In the newest red build [`2081212180027412480`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary/2081212180027412480) (SHA `24a5b063a5`, cos-beta, containerd 2.2.5): ``` Ran 570 of 1283 Specs in 4513.584 seconds FAIL! - Suite Timeout Elapsed ``` `4513s ≈ 75.2 min`. Ginkgo is invoked with `--timeout=75m` (`ginkgo.timeout=1h14m59s`), wrapped in `timeout -k 30s 5400s`. 24 specs report `[TIMEDOUT]` in that single run — the mark of the *suite* clock expiring, not one test hanging. The `context canceled` on `getting pod` is ginkgo tearing the node down, not a kubelet/probe error. **2. Green runs pass with almost no margin.** Recent SUCCESS builds: | Build | Runtime | Budget | |---|---|---| | [`2081296486347313152`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary/2081296486347313152) | 3852s | /4500s | | [`2081233824569626624`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary/2081233824569626624) | 4058s | /4500s | | [`2081191042714963968`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary/2081191042714963968) | **4396s** | /4500s | Green passes land at 85–98 % of budget. Any run a few minutes slower tips over. This is the textbook signature of a suite that has outgrown its timeout — **pass/fail is decided by run-to-run timing noise, not by code correctness.** **3. The suite is growing.** Spec count has climbed steadily: - Jul 12 ([`2076329600698290176`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-node-canary/2076329600698290176)): `will run 581 of 1217 specs` — already timing out - Jul 19–20: `581 of 1224` - Jul 26: `581 of 1283` `+66 total specs in two weeks`, while the 75m budget is unchanged. The failures in this cluster stretch back to **at least Jul 12** — this is chronic capacity exhaustion, **not** an onset tied to a single recent PR. **4. Why probe tests are always the ones caught.** The named specs (`should *not* be restarted …`) call `runLivenessTest` with a **fixed 240 s (4-minute) wait** (`0x37e11d6000` = 240s in the goroutine dump) to prove a restart does *not* happen — `container_probe.go:1806/1819`, sleeping in a `time.Sleep`-driven poll loop (`container_probe.go:1856`). They are among the longest-running specs in the suite, so probabilistically they are the ones in flight when the global clock expires. That's selection bias, not causation — the cluster also sweeps in `containers-lifecycle`, GRPC-probe, and restartable-init specs for the same reason. ### Job config (from `test-infra`) `config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-testing/kubetest-canaries.yaml`: `interval: 1h`, cluster `k8s-infra-prow-build` (real HW, not emulated), `--test_args=--nodes=8 --focus="[NodeConformance]" --skip="[Flaky]|[Serial]"`, outer `--timeout=90m`, inner ginkgo `--timeout=75m`, VM has only **2 CPU / 4 Gi** running 8 parallel ginkgo processes. It's a **canary** job (`kubekins-e2e:latest-master`, `image-config-canary.yaml` → cos-beta), i.e. an early-warning lane — chronic flake here is comparatively low-severity but real. ### Classification **Infrastructure/capacity flake — not a code regression.** No commit-window bisect is warranted: there is no clean green→red boundary (it's been intermittently red since ≥Jul 12), and green/red runs carry unrelated SHAs. The driver is `total NodeConformance runtime ≥ ginkgo 75m budget`, aggravated by steady spec growth and a small (2 CPU) VM. ### Suggested fixes (for SIG Node) - **Raise the ginkgo budget / outer timeout**, or bump parallelism/VM size, so p99 runtime has real headroom (currently <5 % on good runs). - **Or trim/shard** the NodeConformance set on this canary lane, or give the multi-minute "should *not* be restarted" probe specs a tighter observation window. - This will recur and worsen as specs are added — a timeout bump is a stopgap; sharding is the durable fix. I did **not** find an existing tracking issue for the node-canary suite timeout specifically (searched kubernetes/kubernetes) — #140943 appears to be the first. Worth `/sig node` + `/kind flake` and routing to whoever owns the canary lane's timeout budget. *(Read-only triage; nothing was posted or modified.)* --- *🔬 Automated triage on behalf of @dims, generated by Claude with the `k8s-ci-triage` skill. May contain mistakes — verify before acting.* /triage accepted /priority important-longterm i think we are good here now:

title: Graceful node shutdown conflicts with unattended-upgrades package
content:
#### What happened:
setting shutdownGracePeriod: "60s" and shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: "30s" in /etc/kubernetes/kubelet-config.yaml results in /var/log/kubelet.log messages like:
Jun 2 19:41:48 test-c2rtl5620bsn3hi5voeg-kublettest1-default-0000042f kubelet.service[7402]: E0602 19:41:48.214662 7402 kubelet.go:1404] "Failed to start node shutdown manager" err="node shutdown manager was unable to update logind InhibitDelayMaxSec to 1m0s (ShutdownGracePeriod), current value of InhibitDelayMaxSec (30s) is less than requested ShutdownGracePeriod" 

#### What you expected to happen:
I expected the graceful node shutdown configuration settings to take precedence.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
configure graceful node shutdown (shutdownGracePeriod: "60s" and shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: "30s" ) on a node with the unattended-upgrades package installed

check the log for messages indicating "node shutdown manager was unable to update logind InhibitDelayMaxSec ..."

#### Anything else we need to know?:
unattended-upgrades writes /usr/lib/systemd/logind.conf.d/unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf containing InhibitDelayMaxSec=30

the Kubernetes code writes /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/99-kubelet.conf which contains a definition of InhibitDelayMaxSec ultimately based on the values in /etc/kubernetes/kubelet-config.yaml

/usr/lib/systemd/logind.conf.d/unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf has a higher precedence than /etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/99-kubelet.conf so the InhibitDelayMaxSec value in /usr/lib/systemd/logind.conf.d/unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf is used.

for any value other than 30 seconds ... the Kubernetes implementation of GracefulNodeShutdown is incompatible with the unattended-upgrades package

This issue took me an evening to crack, but I seem to have figured it out. The problem resides not in Kubernetes but in the unattended-upgrades package itself.

As stated in logind.conf [documentation](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/logind.conf.html), 

> Files in the *.conf.d/ configuration subdirectories are sorted by their filename in lexicographic order, regardless of in which of the subdirectories they reside.

and

> When multiple files specify the same option, for options which accept just a single value, the entry in the file sorted last takes precedence.

In short, **logind.conf.d directories are treated as a single directory**, and the **option value of the last of sorted files prevails**.

### What is happening?

- Kubernetes creates its `InhibitDelayMaxSec` local override at `/etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/99-kubelet.conf`.
- unattended-upgrades creates its `InhibitDelayMaxSec` local override at `/usr/lib/systemd/logind.conf.d/unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf`.
- When sorted, `unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf` becomes the last of sorted files and overrides `99-kubelet.conf`.

By ignoring login.conf documentation recommendation

> to use the range 10-40 for drop-ins in /usr/ and the range 60-90 for drop-ins in /etc/ and /run/, to make sure that local and transient drop-ins take priority over drop-ins shipped by the OS vendor,

unattended-upgrades package caused this and probably some other issues where `InhibitDelayMaxSec` overrides were needed.

### How this issue can be resolved?

#### For the current setups

> To disable a configuration file supplied by the vendor, the recommended way is to place a symlink to /dev/null in the configuration directory in /etc/, with the same filename as the vendor configuration file.

e. g. create `/etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf -> /dev/null` symlink.

#### In the long run

`unattended-upgrades` package must change its logind.conf local override to include the prefix recommended above (e. g. `10-unattended-upgrades-logind-maxdelay.conf`).

## Triage: `ci-kubernetes-ec2-conformance-latest` — deployer panic, not a k8s regression

**Verdict: infrastructure/tooling bug in the external AWS deployer (`kubetest2-ec2`), not a kubernetes/kubernetes test regression.** The e2e suite never runs — the job dies during cluster bring-up.

### Root cause: `panic: send on closed channel` in the deployer

Every recent red build fails identically, before any test executes, with a Go panic in the AWS provider's `Up()`:

```
panic: send on closed channel
sigs.k8s.io/provider-aws-test-infra/kubetest2-ec2@v0.0.0-20260725022349-98b606df218a/pkg/deployer/up.go:152
created by ...deployer.(*deployer).Up
	.../pkg/deployer/up.go:144
+ EXIT_VALUE=1
```

This is a classic **concurrency race** in [`pkg/deployer/up.go`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra/blob/98b606df218a/kubetest2-ec2/pkg/deployer/up.go#L120-L168):

- Each instance-readiness goroutine does `fatalErrors <- err` on error (line 152).
- The main goroutine `select`s on `wgDone` vs `fatalErrors`; on the **first** error it takes the `fatalErrors` case and immediately `close(fatalErrors)` (line 167) then returns.
- If a **second** instance goroutine then tries `fatalErrors <- err` on the now-closed channel → `send on closed channel` → panic. The unbuffered channel + `close()` on an error path is the bug. This job provisions multiple EC2 instances (control plane + workers), so >1 goroutine failing in the same run is exactly what trips it.

`finished.json` = `FAILURE`, and the build log contains **zero** Ginkgo suite markers — confirming the conformance tests never started. The trailing SSH "command not found" / "admin.conf: no such file" errors are just `DumpClusterLogs()` running against half-provisioned nodes after the failure — noise, not the cause.

### This is NOT a version regression — same deployer SHA is green and red

The job does `go install sigs.k8s.io/provider-aws-test-infra/kubetest2-ec2@latest`. The **identical** resolved version `v0.0.0-20260725022349-98b606df218a` (commit `98b606df218a`, 2026-07-25) appears in both **SUCCESS and FAILURE** builds:

| Build | Started | Result | Deployer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2081624404407619584 | Jul 27 06:15 | ✅ SUCCESS | `...98b606df218a` |
| 2081352352782094336 | Jul 26 12:14 | ✅ SUCCESS | `...98b606df218a` |
| [2081715248577908736](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-ec2-conformance-latest/2081715248577908736) | Jul 27 12:16 | ❌ panic | `...98b606df218a` |
| [2081987294574678016](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-ec2-conformance-latest/2081987294574678016) | Jul 28 06:17 | ❌ panic | `...98b606df218a` |

Because the code is bit-identical across pass and fail, this is an **intermittent race that only fires when ≥2 instances error during provisioning** (typically flaky EC2 capacity/SSH bring-up), not a change that can be bisected in the k8s commit window. The k8s SHA is irrelevant to the failure.

### On the "since Jul 13" claim

The issue's "first failure Jul 13" aggregates *any* red build under the "Build failed outside of test results" bucket, which lumps together distinct infra failures. The current streak (Jul 27 12:16 onward, 4 consecutive) is the `send on closed channel` panic. Earlier reds were different infra flakes — e.g. build [2081261507026358272](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-ec2-conformance-latest/2081261507026358272) (Jul 26) had **no panic**; it failed with `stat /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf: no such file` (kubeadm init didn't complete) and `exit status 255`. So the "Overall" test has been noisy from multiple independent provisioning issues, with the panic being the newest and now-dominant one.

### Recommendation

This belongs in **kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra**, not kubernetes/kubernetes. No open issue/PR mentions `send on closed channel` there yet (searched, none found). The fix is in the deployer's `Up()`:

- Don't `close(fatalErrors)` while other goroutines may still send. Use a **buffered** channel sized to the instance count, or a `sync.Once`/`context` cancellation instead of closing, or collect errors via `errgroup`. The `close(fatalErrors)` at [up.go:167](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra/blob/98b606df218a/kubetest2-ec2/pkg/deployer/up.go#L167) should be removed.

Suggested next step: **/sig cloud-provider** to hand off, and file/track the deployer bug against `kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra`. No k8s revert is warranted — this job cannot be fixed by any change in this repo. (Since the panic is load/timing dependent, retries will occasionally go green, which is why the job flaps rather than staying solid red.)

## Triage: job is red because the **ubuntu-2404 EC2 instance intermittently fails to start containerd**, not a test/code failure

**TL;DR** — This is not a Kubernetes regression and not a failing test. The job runs the NodeConformance suite against **two images in parallel**, and one of them (`ubuntu-2404`) intermittently comes up without containerd. When that instance never reaches a running `containerd`/`crio` service, the AWS runner aborts *that image's* suite and returns a non-zero exit, which reddens the whole job — even though every spec that actually ran passed. This is an **infrastructure/environment flake in `kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra`**, and it matches the issue title exactly ("instances failing after running test successfully").

### Evidence

The job initializes two images per run:
```
Initializing e2e tests using image al2023-6-1  / ami-0006118602dfc1c09.   → SUCCESS! 430 Passed | 0 Failed
Initializing e2e tests using image ubuntu-2404 / ami-084568db4383264d4.   → never starts
```

The al2023 host runs the full suite cleanly. The ubuntu-2404 host boots and is SSH-reachable, but `systemctl list-units --state=running | grep -e containerd -e crio` returns nothing for **~50 retries over ~15 min**, then the runner gives up ([build-log.txt](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-ec2/2082133011318444032/build-log.txt)):
```
Failure Finished Test Suite on Host . Refer to artifacts directory for ginkgo log for this host.
unable to create EC2 instance for image ami-084568db4383264d4, instance i-05b12e6cca85d0481
  is not running, instance i-05b12e6cca85d0481 not running containerd/crio daemon - Command failed:
...
SUCCESS! -- 430 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 849 Skipped   ← the al2023 image
Failure: 1 errors encountered.                                ← the ubuntu image → EXIT_VALUE=1
```
No artifacts/junit are captured for the failed host — only the al2023 host has a `junit_*.xml` — which is why TestGrid shows "the overall job red" with no individual failing test.

### This is the same failure on every red build, and it's intermittent

Same pinned AMI `ami-084568db4383264d4` (the ubuntu ssm_path is snapshot-pinned to `.../20250305/...`, so it never rotates), different instance ID each time:

| Build | ubuntu-2404 outcome | al2023 outcome |
|---|---|---|
| [2082133011318444032](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-ec2/2082133011318444032) (07-28) | ❌ containerd never up (`i-05b12e6…`) | ✅ 430 passed |
| [2082042160084946944](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-ec2/2082042160084946944) | ❌ (`i-02a2c3d…`) | ✅ 430 passed |
| [2081951310877298688](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-ec2/2081951310877298688) | ❌ (`i-0644d7e…`) | ✅ 430 passed |
| [2081860709058088960](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-ec2/2081860709058088960) (**green**) | ✅ **434 passed** | ✅ 430 passed |

The **same AMI runs 434 specs successfully** in green builds — so the ubuntu image is not fundamentally broken; containerd start-up is failing *intermittently* (~50–60% of runs since ~07-27). The `ci-containerd-node-e2e-serial-ec2` job shows the identical intermittent SUCCESS/FAILURE alternation.

### Ruling out a k8s regression (empty commit window)

Both the last-green and first-red builds carry the **same** `kubernetes/kubernetes` commit — `started.json` `repo-commit=98b606df218a2138e908eeeb473d0d6610922a56` on both. The commit window is empty, so no k/k PR is responsible. The job is driven by `kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra@main`, whose most recent change ([#577, "Bump k8s"](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra/pull/577)) merged **2026-07-25**, before the ~07-27 onset — so no test-infra config change lines up either. On ubuntu-2404 the runner builds **containerd + runc from `main` at HEAD** via `containerd-installation.service`, so the most likely moving part is the upstream containerd-main build/startup on Ubuntu 24.04, or transient AWS/network flake during that install.

### Classification & suggested next steps

**Infrastructure flake, not a code regression / not a failing test.** No k/k or provider-aws-test-infra revert is warranted.

To pin down *why* containerd doesn't start on ubuntu-2404, the runner should be made to **capture logs from the failed host before terminating it** — today the instance is torn down with zero artifacts, so `containerd-installation.service` / cloud-init output is lost. Concretely:
- In the AWS runner, on the "not running containerd/crio daemon" path, SSH `journalctl -u containerd-installation -u containerd` + `cloud-init.log` off the instance into artifacts before terminate.
- Given it's ubuntu-specific and containerd-from-`main`, this most likely lives with SIG Node's containerd node-e2e / `kubernetes-sigs/provider-aws-test-infra` owners (@dims, cc SIG Node CI).

I found no separate tracking issue beyond #141013 itself.

title: A potential data conflict occurs in cert_rotation.go
content:
clientCert is read/written 4 times in cert_rotation.go; 3 out of 4 times it is protected by c.certMtx.RLock()/Lock(),which is in L76、L77、L84; 1 out of 4 times it is read without a Lock, which is in [L97](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/cert_rotation.go#L79)

> 	c.certMtx.RLock()
	haveCert := c.clientCert != nil
	if certsEqual(c.clientCert, cert) {
		c.certMtx.RUnlock()
		return c.clientCert, nil
	}
	c.certMtx.RUnlock()

In the above code, I think it would be better to first store c.clientCert in a temporary variable and then return it.

> 	c.certMtx.RLock()
	haveCert := c.clientCert != nil
	if certsEqual(c.clientCert, cert) {
                temp:=c.clientCert
		c.certMtx.RUnlock()
		return temp, nil
	}
	c.certMtx.RUnlock()

Excuse me, how do you view this issue? I'm looking forward to your reply.

The mutex guards a pointer type variable. 

The pointer variable is only written to by updating the pointer, not by de-referencing and writing to the underlying object.

The referenced code returns the pointer value.

I don't think there's any data conflict, though this isn't how I'd write mutex code in go.

The purpose of this mutex seems to be ensuring that we are able to diff before/after updating the client cert so we know if we need to close connections.

This is a real data race and it just failed our CI, so I'd like to add a concrete trace to the report.

Re [the earlier assessment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134876#issuecomment-3502627562) that there is no conflict because the mutex only guards a pointer: the problem isn't the pointee, it's the *variable*. `loadClientCert` reads `c.clientCert` **after** releasing the read lock:

https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/transport/cert_rotation.go#L75-L85

```go
c.certMtx.RLock()
haveCert := c.clientCert != nil
if certsEqual(c.clientCert, cert) {
	c.certMtx.RUnlock()
	return c.clientCert, nil   // <-- unsynchronized read
}
c.certMtx.RUnlock()

c.certMtx.Lock()
c.clientCert = cert            // <-- concurrent write
c.certMtx.Unlock()
```

An unsynchronized read concurrently with a write of the same variable is a data race under the Go memory model, independent of what the pointer points to. It is benign in practice on amd64/arm64 (word-sized loads and stores don't tear), but it is still a race the detector reports, which means it fails any `go test -race` build that exercises this path.

Observed with client-go v0.36.3 / Go 1.26.5 on linux-amd64, in an e2e suite that talks to a minikube cluster (kubeconfig with `client-certificate`/`client-key` file paths, so `ReloadTLSFiles` is set and the rotation goroutine is started). The rotation worker and a TLS handshake hit the two lines above concurrently:

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0001eac18 by goroutine 1771:
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).loadClientCert()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:84 +0xfb
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).GetClientCertificate()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:179 +0x2e
  crypto/tls.(*Conn).getClientCertificate()
      crypto/tls/handshake_client.go:1266 +0x10e
  crypto/tls.(*clientHandshakeStateTLS13).sendClientCertificate()
      crypto/tls/handshake_client_tls13.go:748 +0x434
  ...
  net/http.(*persistConn).addTLS.func2()
      net/http/transport.go:1736 +0x93

Previous read at 0x00c0001eac18 by goroutine 24:
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).loadClientCert()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:79 +0x22e
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).processNextWorkItem()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:166 +0x152
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).runWorker()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:155 +0x2e
  ...
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).run.gowrap4()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:144 +0xe

Goroutine 24 (running) created at:
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*dynamicClientCert).run()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cert_rotation.go:144 +0x40a
  k8s.io/client-go/transport.(*tlsTransportCache).get.gowrap2()
      k8s.io/client-go@v0.36.3/transport/cache.go:139 +0x38
```

The whole test binary fails with `race detected during execution of test`, with no frame from the consuming project — so from a user's perspective this is an unattributable flake.

A minimal fix that keeps the existing semantics is to read the pointer once while the lock is held:

```go
c.certMtx.RLock()
currentCert := c.clientCert
haveCert := currentCert != nil
if certsEqual(currentCert, cert) {
	c.certMtx.RUnlock()
	return currentCert, nil
}
c.certMtx.RUnlock()
```

Happy to open a PR if that direction is acceptable.

title: CreateContainerError when secret env var contains invalid UTF-8 bytes (gRPC strict validation regression)
content:
### What happened?

Pods fail with `CreateContainerError` and the following event (events.k8s.io/v1) message:

```
Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

When an environment variable sourced from a Kubernetes Secret contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The kubelet passes the raw secret bytes as a protobuf `string` field in the CRI `CreateContainerRequest` to containerd. Since gRPC v1.72+ (bundled in k8s 1.34) enforces strict UTF-8 validation on `string` fields, the container creation is rejected.

This is distinct from #136323 / #136325 which fixed env var *expansion* truncating multi-byte UTF-8 characters. That fix does not address this case - here the secret value itself contains raw bytes that were never valid UTF-8 in the first place.

The same pods work on kubelet v1.33.7 nodes in the same cluster because the older gRPC version did not enforce UTF-8 validation on string fields. This is a silent behavioral regression with no warning or migration path.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:

1. The kubelet should validate secret values for UTF-8 correctness before sending them over CRI gRPC, and emit a clear warning/event identifying which env var contains the invalid value.
2. The CRI protobuf definition should use `bytes` instead of `string` for env var values (since secrets are fundamentally binary).
3. At minimum, the error message should identify which specific environment variable contains the invalid UTF-8, rather than the opaque gRPC marshaling error.

Currently there is no indication of which env var is problematic, making debugging difficult.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# 1. Create a secret containing invalid UTF-8 bytes
#    \xc3\x28 is an incomplete UTF-8 sequence (0xC3 expects a continuation byte 0x80-0xBF, not 0x28)
python3 -c "
import base64
invalid_bytes = b'hello\xc3\x28world'
encoded = base64.b64encode(invalid_bytes).decode()
manifest = f'''apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: utf8-invalid-secret
  namespace: default
data:
  test-key: {encoded}
'''
print(manifest)
" | kubectl apply -f -

# 2. Create a pod that uses this secret as an env var
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: utf8-test-invalid
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: BAD_VAR
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: utf8-invalid-secret
          key: test-key
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF

# 3. Observe the pod enters CreateContainerError
kubectl get pod utf8-test-invalid
# NAME                READY   STATUS                 RESTARTS   AGE
# utf8-test-invalid   0/1     CreateContainerError   0          14s

kubectl describe pod utf8-test-invalid | grep -A2 "Warning.*Failed"
# Warning  Failed  kubelet  Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

Note: The same secret and pod spec works without error on k8s 1.33 nodes (older gRPC without strict UTF-8 enforcement).

### Anything else we need to know?

Partially redacted warning events:

<details>
```yaml
apiVersion: events.k8s.io/v1
kind: Event
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: <redacted>
  name: <redacted>
  namespace: <redacted>
  resourceVersion: <redacted>
  uid: <redacted>
note: 'Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8'
reason: Failed
regarding:
  apiVersion: v1
  fieldPath: spec.containers{<redacted>}
  kind: Pod
  name: <redacted>
  namespace: <redacted>
  resourceVersion: <redacted>
  uid: <redacted>
reportingController: kubelet
reportingInstance: aks-<redacted>
type: Warning
```
</details>

### Kubernetes version

$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.36.1
Kustomize Version: v5.8.1
Server Version: v1.34.6
```

My plan is to add UTF-8 validation in makeEnvironmentVariables() in pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go before the CRI call, and surface a clear error event identifying the specific env var name and secret source that contains invalid bytes. Will check in on #sig-node Slack before opening a PR.

Will check in on #sig-node Slack before opening a PR.

Thanks for looking into this, @Kartavyasonar! What are your thoughts on option 2?

>The CRI protobuf definition should use bytes instead of string for env var values (since secrets are fundamentally binary).

Ref. https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configmap-secret/managing-secret-using-config-file/ and the following description:

>The data field is used to store arbitrary data, encoded using base64.

Would not classifying this as invalid also be to introduce a breaking change to the v1.Secret API?

There was a recent discussion about the rest-API pod side of this and avoiding breaking changes.

cc @dims @liggitt maybe we can re-relax just the gRPC part without changing the types ...

> > I'd like to work on this. My plan is to add UTF-8 validation in makeEnvironmentVariables() in pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go before the CRI call, and surface a clear error event identifying the specific env var name and secret source that contains invalid bytes. Will check in on #sig-node Slack before opening a PR.
> 
> Thanks for looking into this, [@Kartavyasonar](https://github.com/Kartavyasonar)! What are your thoughts on option 2?
> 
> > The CRI protobuf definition should use bytes instead of string for env var values (since secrets are fundamentally binary).
> 
> Ref. https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configmap-secret/managing-secret-using-config-file/ and the following description:
> 
> > The data field is used to store arbitrary data, encoded using base64.
> 
> Would not classifying this as invalid also be to introduce a breaking change to the v1.Secret API?

Thanks for the context @tnn-simon. You're right that Secret.data is explicitly documented as storing arbitrary data encoded as base64, which means non-UTF-8 bytes are a completely valid use case validating them out in kubelet would be a breaking change for legitimate workloads.
Given @BenTheElder's comment about re-relaxing the gRPC validation, I think the correct fix is at the gRPC/protobuf layer rather than in makeEnvironmentVariables(). I'll hold off on writing code until @dims or @liggitt weigh in on the preferred direction.

Env var spec
  * Values may contain binary data but must not contain a null byte (disallowing the null byte means that environment variables _already_ cannot handle all values that could be stored in a secret, and we should improve detecting / handling that scenario more gracefully)

Env var handling
  * Depending on the pipeline the value is going through, binary values may or may not be transmitted successfully or losslessly

CRI
  * Binary data in env values was _always_ disallowed by the cri-api spec (it specs the envvar value as a `string` which is defined as being utf-8)
  * Binary data was _accidentally_ allowed on the encoding side (in the kubelet) by missing validation in gogo protobuf
  * Starting in 1.34, the kubelet switched to use standard protobuf encoding library, which strictly validated
  * Whether binary data was supported in a _particular_ container runtime depended on what proto library they used and whether it validated according to the cri-api proto definition as a string


Options I see:
1. Change cri-api from `string value` to `bytes value`. This serializes identically in proto but drops the utf-8 requirement.
   * This moves kubelet behavior back to match pre-1.34 behavior.
   * Whether a particular container runtime or pipeline will actually support binary values with fidelity is still unclear.
   * Still need to validate and reject null bytes in values in the kubelet, which means arbitrary binary data still cannot be reliably placed in Secrets for use as envvars.
   * 1.34, 1.35, 1.36 kubelets will still error on non-utf-8 data (I think the cri-api and kubelet change to treat values as `[]byte` is too invasive to backport)

2. Validate all env values are utf-8 and don't contain the NUL byte, error in the kubelet if they are not, and document a recommendation to do application-level encoding/decoding of binary values to pass through envvars (like base64 encoding, etc).
   * This is more consistent with envvar portability recommendations (from https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/000095399/basedefs/xbd_chap08.html: `For values to be portable across systems conforming to IEEE Std 1003.1-2001, the value shall be composed of characters from the portable character set (except NUL and as indicated below)`).
   * Stays consistent with cri-api spec of the value as a string
   * Stays more consistent with 1.34, 1.35, 1.36 behavior
   * Guides implementers to approaches that are more likely to work with any container runtime and pipeline

~~I think I'm in favor of keeping the cri-api as-is, and preventing propagation of envvar values with non-utf8 or nul bytes in the kubelet~~

title: Exec readiness probes silently broken during graceful pod termination since v1.35 (probe context canceled at teardown)
content:
### What happened?

Since v1.35.0, exec readiness probes stop working the moment a pod begins graceful termination. Every probe attempt fails client-side with `rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled`, the prober discards errored results, and the pod's `Ready` condition stays frozen at whatever it was before termination began. A pod whose readiness probe starts failing during its grace period is never marked NotReady.

This is a regression from #130487 (`chore(kubelet): migrate prober to contextual logging`, commit b6f6731ab61, first released in v1.35.0). Probe workers previously ran on `context.Background()`. They now inherit the pod worker's sync context via `probeManager.AddPod(ctx, pod)` in `kubelet.SyncPod`, and `pod_workers.go` cancels that context as soon as teardown begins ("Cancelling current pod sync"). Every subsequent CRI `ExecSync` fails immediately. In a 60s grace period I logged 61 consecutive canceled probes.

Only exec probes are affected. The HTTP, TCP, and gRPC probers don't take the ctx.

### What did you expect to happen?

Readiness probes keep running during graceful termination, and a failing probe flips the pod Ready condition to False within a few probe periods. This worked before 1.35 (see the delete-path output in #124648, filed against ~1.30, where READY drops during Terminating).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Pod with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60` running busybox with a script that touches `/tmp/ready`, traps TERM to `rm -f /tmp/ready; sleep 300`, and idles. Readiness probe: exec `cat /tmp/ready`, `periodSeconds: 1`, `failureThreshold: 1`.

1. Wait for Ready=True.
2. `kubectl delete pod <pod>` and sample `.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status` once per second.

Observed on kindest/node:v1.35.0: Ready stays True for the entire 59s until the containers die. Kubelet events show `Readiness probe errored and resulted in unknown state: rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled` repeating once per probe period (capped at 25 by event spam filtering).

Note: assert on the pod Ready condition, not the EndpointSlice. The deletionTimestamp withdraws the endpoint immediately regardless of readiness, which masks the bug.

### Anything else we need to know?

Mechanism, confirmed at `--v=4`:

1. `pod_workers.go` cancels the pod sync context at teardown start (`status.cancelFn()`, "Cancelling current pod sync").
2. Probe workers were started with that context (`kl.probeManager.AddPod(ctx, pod)` in `SyncPod`; `go w.run(ctx)` in `prober_manager.go`). Ironically this call site sits right above the #113606 TODO warning about exactly this class of problem.
3. `runProbe` passes the ctx into `newExecInContainer`, so `ExecSync` fails instantly with grpc `Canceled`.
4. `worker.doProbe` treats probe errors as "throw away the result", so `results.Failure` is never recorded and `SetContainerReadiness` never fires.

E0723 15:14:06.482925   73978 prober.go:106] "Probe errored" err="rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled" probeType="Readiness" pod="default/ready-test-847548cb79-svk98" podUID="9550856e-f6bd-4a14-b7af-9c2a1f8b7ece" containerName="app" probeResult="unknown"
I0723 15:14:07.483364   73978 prober.go:156] "Exec-Probe runProbe" pod="default/ready-test-847548cb79-svk98" containerName="app" execCommand=["cat","/tmp/ready"]
I0723 15:14:07.483874   73978 prober.go:156] "Exec-Probe runProbe" pod="default/ready-test-847548cb79-svk98" containerName="app" execCommand=["cat","/tmp/ready"]
I0723 15:14:07.484279   73978 prober.go:156] "Exec-Probe runProbe" pod="default/ready-test-847548cb79-svk98" containerName="app" execCommand=["cat","/tmp/ready"]
E0723 15:14:07.484409   73978 prober.go:106] "Probe errored" err="rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled" probeType="Readiness" pod="default/ready-test-847548cb79-svk98" podUID="9550856e-f6bd-4a14-b7af-9c2a1f8b7ece" containerName="app" probeResult="unknown"
```

The three `Exec-Probe runProbe` lines per tick are `runProbeWithRetries` (3 attempts). The pattern repeats once per second for the entire grace period: 61 canceled probes total, zero successful or failed results recorded.

</details>

Verified fix: `go w.run(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))` at the three call sites in `prober_manager.go AddPod`. Worker lifetime is already managed by its own stop channel; `WithoutCancel` keeps the logger. With that two-line change on v1.35.0, the same repro flips Ready to False 1s after the delete. Test matrix (same kind node, kubelet binary swapped):

| kubelet | Ready during 60s graceful delete |
|---|---|
| stock v1.35.0 | True the whole time (bug) |
| v1.35.0 + #139167 | True the whole time (unchanged) |
| v1.35.0 + `WithoutCancel` fix | False at 1s |

Related: this is the dominant cause behind #124648's symptom on current versions, and it makes #139167 a no-op as written (its new branch is gated on phase Failed/Succeeded, which a gracefully deleted pod never hits while containers run; on the eviction path its extra probes hit the same canceled context). The `ready = !workerExists` latching issue described by @smarterclayton on #116965 is real but only reachable once this is fixed. No e2e covers readiness during pod deletion; the merged "readiness probe while in preStop" NodeConformance test only exercises the liveness-kill path, where no teardown occurs, which is how this shipped green. PR to follow.

title: E2E Test Flakiness: API Server Timeouts, Silent Failures, and Resource Cleanup Issues
content:
The e2e test framework has several patterns that cause flakiness, silent resource leaks, and hard-to-debug failures, especially in disruptive tests that restart API servers or control plane components. PR 137832 addresses these across 13 files (185 additions, 41 deletions), touching SIG api-machinery, apps, cloud-provider, network, node, storage, and testing.

Error suppression hides resource leaks. Across the test suite, cleanup code discards errors from Delete calls. In test/e2e/apimachinery/aggregator.go, the cleanupSampleAPIServer function has 10 such calls (APIService, Deployment, Secret, Service, ServiceAccount, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding, ClusterRole) all silently swallowed. Same pattern in test/e2e/apimachinery/apply.go (4 deployments/pods), test/e2e/apps/rc.go (DeleteCollection), and test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go (ConfigMaps in defer blocks). When these fail, resources leak into subsequent tests with zero trace of what went wrong.

No retry on transient API server errors. GetControlPlaneNodes in test/e2e/framework/util.go calls Nodes().List() and immediately fails on any error. During disruptive tests (daemon restarts, etcd failure injection), the API server is expected to be briefly unreachable. The same issue exists in allNodesReady at test/e2e/framework/node/helper.go and RestartNodes at test/e2e/common/util.go. A transient connection refused or 503 kills the entire test instead of retrying. The fix introduces IsRetryableAPIError which checks for connection refused/reset, server timeout, 429, 503, 500, and unexpected server errors, plus a new WaitForControlPlaneNodes that wraps the listing in a polling loop with retry-on-transient logic.

Healthz returns 200 before daemon is ready. RestartDaemonConfig.waitUp in test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go considers the daemon ready when /healthz returns HTTP 200. After a kubelet restart, the health endpoint can report ok while kubelet is still recovering. Logs show errors, pods are not yet scheduled. The fix adds verifyDaemonReadiness which SSHes into the node and checks the last 20 lines of /var/log/kubelet.log for error patterns before declaring readiness.

Goroutines not gracefully stopped. In test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go, a cache.NewInformer controller is started with go controller.Run(backgroundCtx.Done()). The cleanup calls cancel() but does not wait for the controller goroutine to finish. The fix replaces this with a dedicated stopCh channel and DeferCleanup that closes the channel then sleeps 100ms to allow graceful shutdown.

PVC deletion races with pod references. DeleteAllStatefulSets in test/e2e/framework/statefulset/rest.go has a TODO comment about not checking whether pods still reference PVCs before deleting them. The current code deletes PVCs immediately, which can fail or leave orphaned PVs when pods are still running. The fix lists pods, checks volume references, and only deletes PVCs that are not in use, with foreground propagation.

Duplicated control plane filtering. GetControlPlaneNodes and WaitForControlPlaneNodes both contain the same node filtering logic (check for control-plane label and NoSchedule taint). The second commit extracts this into a shared filterControlPlaneNodes helper.

All changes are in e2e test code, no user-facing impact.

Related issues:
- 109600: prevent the Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred()) and ExpectNoError(err) anti-pattern in e2e tests (same category of error handling problems)
- 86253: sample-apiserver returns error instead of falling back to second Accept type (directly affects the aggregator.go test modified in this PR)
- 135285: GOAWAY are not handled gracefully in apiserver when aggregating (related network error handling)
- 105536: Orphaned pod found, but error not a directory occurred when trying to remove the volumes dir (related resource cleanup issue)

title: client-go: FakeCustomStore no longer implements cache.Store after #134827
content:
### What happened?

#134827 (merged 2025-10-23, shipped in client-go v0.36) added two methods to the `cache.Store` interface:

- `Bookmark(rv string)`
- `LastStoreSyncResourceVersion() string`

The package's own test double `cache.FakeCustomStore` (`staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/fake_custom_store.go`) was not updated, so it no longer satisfies `cache.Store`. Downstream test code that passes a `FakeCustomStore` where a `Store` is expected now fails to compile:

```
cannot use &cache.FakeCustomStore{...} (value of type *cache.FakeCustomStore) as cache.Store value:
	*cache.FakeCustomStore does not implement cache.Store (missing method Bookmark)
```

We hit this in the wild during KubeVirt's bump to v0.36.2 (kubevirt/kubevirt#18315) and had to add a local wrapper to keep ~10 test files compiling.

### What did you expect to happen?

`FakeCustomStore` keeps satisfying `cache.Store`. It is named and documented as a general store fake ("lets you define custom functions for store operations") and has satisfied `Store` since 2016. The new narrower `ReflectorStore` interface is not a substitute for read-path consumers (it has no `List`/`GetByKey`), and #134827 carried no deprecation signal for the fake.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```go
package main

import "k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache"

var _ cache.Store = &cache.FakeCustomStore{} // fails to compile with client-go v0.36.x
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Proposed fix (~15 lines, backward compatible): add `BookmarkFunc func(rv string)` and `LastStoreSyncResourceVersionFunc func() string` fields plus the two delegating methods (no-op / `""` when nil), matching the file's existing pattern. Happy to submit the PR.

### Kubernetes version

client-go v0.36.x (still present on master as of 2026-07-27)

/sig api-machinery
/kind bug
